summary: Describes a way to specify a service in addition to the mobile node identity in Mobile IPv6, for providers offering several services to one subscriber. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5149 adds a way for a mobile device to name the service it wants when it registers with its home agent. The home agent then checks that the subscriber is allowed to have that service and applies the rules that belong to it.

questions: how to choose service in mobile ipv6
how to select service in mipv6
how does mobile ipv6 service selection work
subtitle: Letting one Mobile IPv6 subscriber ask its home agent for one named service out of several.

tldr.problem: In some Mobile IPv6 deployments, the identity of the mobile node or of the mobility subscription is not enough to tell apart several services provisioned to that same subscription.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines a Service Selection Mobility Option, type 20, that a mobile node puts in a Binding Update to name the service it wants. The home agent checks that the node is authorized for that service and applies the matching policy.
tldr.outcome: The option is sent to the home agent only, not to correspondent nodes, and it may change the home address, the routing and the quality of service applied to the session.

Default service when none is named

today: RFC 5149 is an Informational document and is not listed as obsoleted or updated. It defines a Service Selection Mobility Option for Mobile IPv6 and records the two IANA assignments it received: option type 20 and the home agent status code 151.

sections.title: Introduction and Motivation
sections.content:
Mobile IPv6 can identify mobile nodes in several ways: with home addresses, with Network Access Identifiers (NAIs), or with credentials suitable for IKEv2. In some deployments, identifying the mobile node, or the mobility service subscriber through a Proxy Mobile IPv6 client, is not enough to distinguish between several services that may have been provisioned to that mobile node and its mobility service subscription.

The ability to name a service in addition to the mobile node identity gives a mobility service provider flexibility to run several services inside one mobility service subscription. The document lists the cases this is meant to cover: enterprise data access, where the provider hosts connectivity and mobility services on behalf of the enterprise; access to service domains that are otherwise unreachable from public networks for the provider's own business reasons; simultaneous access to different service domains separated by the provider's policies; and easier assignment of policy and quality of service based on the subscribed services.

When no service is named, the home agent MUST act as if the default service, plain Internet access, had been requested. There is no absolute requirement that this default be available to every subscriber, but it is highly RECOMMENDED, so that ordinary subscribers do not have to configure operator-specific values just to get basic service. The document also warns that picking a service can restrict access to other services, for instance when the services sit in different administrative domains or in customer networks that filter traffic heavily.
sections.plainLanguage: A provider can sell one subscriber several different services. The problem is that Mobile IPv6 normally identifies only the subscriber, so the home agent has no way to tell which service a registration is asking for. This document adds a short field that carries the service name.

sections.title: The Service Selection Mobility Option
sections.content:
At most one Service Selection Mobility Option MAY be included in any Binding Update message. If the Binding Update carries any authorization-related options, such as the Binding Authorization Data option, or any authentication-related options, such as the Mobility Message Authentication option, the Service Selection option MUST appear before them.

The option SHOULD NOT be sent to a correspondent node, because the mobile node cannot assume that the correspondent node knows anything about a service selection made between the mobile node and the home agent. The option itself has no alignment requirement.

The option has three fields. Type is an 8-bit identifier set to 20, the type of a skipable mobility option. Length is an 8-bit unsigned integer giving the length of the option in octets, excluding the Type and Length fields themselves; a value of zero is not allowed. Identifier is a variable-length encoded service identifier string, between 1 and 255 octets long, identifying the requested service. The identifier may be an international string built on Unicode characters, encoded as UTF-8 and formatted using Normalization Form KC (NFKC). The document gives 'ims', 'voip' and 'voip.companyxyz.example.com' as valid examples. At minimum, the identifier MUST be unique among the home agents to which the mobile node is authorized to register.
sections.plainLanguage: The option is a type number of 20, a length byte, and the service name itself. The name is between 1 and 255 bytes long and may be written in any script, as long as it is encoded in UTF-8 and put into a standard Unicode form so that two spellings of the same name match.

sections.title: How Each Node Processes the Option
sections.content:
At the mobile node, the option is used to identify the service associated with the binding registration and SHOULD only be included in the initial Binding Update sent to the home agent. To change the selected service, the mobile node is RECOMMENDED to de-register the existing binding before registering for the new one. Provisioning the service identifiers to the mobile node or Proxy Mobile IPv6 client is out of scope. When present, the option MUST appear after the Mobile Node-Network Access Identifier option, if that one is present, and before any authorization or authentication options. It works with any mobile node identification method, whether a home address, an MN-NAI or credentials suitable for IKEv2.

If the mobile node receives a Binding Acknowledgement with the status code SERVICE_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED and it already has a binding with the Home Address or Home Network Prefix used in the failed Binding Update, the mobile node MUST delete that existing binding. If there is no existing binding, it proceeds as with any failed initial binding registration.

At the home agent, receiving a Binding Update with a Service Selection option means the home agent authenticates and authorizes the mobile node as usual, and, if it supports Service Selection, it MUST also verify that the mobile node is authorized for the service named in the option. The services a node is authorized for SHOULD be part of its general subscription profile. If the node is not authorized, the home agent MUST deny the registration and send a Binding Acknowledgement with the status code SERVICE_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED (151).

Beyond authorization, the option MAY affect the Home Address or Home Network Prefix allocation, for example when used with the MN-NAI option, where the same NAI may map to different Home Addresses or Home Network Prefixes depending on the service. It MAY also affect how the home agent routes outbound IP packets, and the home agent MAY apply different policy or quality of service treatment based on the selected service. If the new Binding Update changes the selected service, the home agent MUST re-authorize the node. If that authorization fails, the home agent MUST deny the registration, delete any binding with the existing Home Address or Home Network Prefix, and send the same status code.

At the correspondent node, the option is more or less useless unless the correspondent node and the home agent share the same knowledge about mobility services, in which case the correspondent node SHOULD silently ignore it. Where both belong to the same administrative domain, the correspondent node may share the home agent's knowledge and provide service-based traffic handling to mobile nodes.
sections.plainLanguage: The mobile node names the service when it registers. The home agent checks the subscription, and if the name is not allowed it refuses the registration and reports the refusal with a status code. The chosen service can also change the address the node is given, how its packets are routed, and the quality of service it receives.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The protection for the Service Selection Mobility Option depends on the service being identified and eventually selected. If the service selection information should not be revealed on the wire, Binding Updates and Binding Acknowledgements should use Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) in transport mode with a non-null encryption transform, so that the messages carry confidentiality as well as integrity.
sections.plainLanguage: The security of the option depends on the service it names. When the name should stay private, the registration messages should be encrypted with ESP in transport mode.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: A new Mobile IPv6 Mobility Option type was assigned for the option described in the document: the Service Selection Mobility Option is set to 20. A new Mobile IPv6 registration denied by home agent Status Code was also assigned, from the range 128-255: SERVICE_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED is set to 151.
sections.plainLanguage: Two numbers were registered for this work: the option type 20, and the status code 151 that a home agent sends when it refuses a service it is not authorized to grant.

viz.caption: SERVICE SELECTION MOBILITY OPTION IN ITS SHORTEST FORM

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Set to 20, the type of a skipable mobility option.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length of the option in octets, excluding the Type and Length fields. A value of zero is not allowed.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.desc: Service identifier string, 1 to 255 octets, UTF-8 encoded and in Unicode Normalization Form KC.

viz.caption: THE CASES THE OPTION IS MEANT TO COVER

items.title: Enterprise access
items.text: The provider hosts connectivity and mobility services on behalf of an enterprise.

items.title: Restricted service domains
items.text: Access to service domains that are not reachable from public networks for the provider's own reasons.

items.title: Simultaneous access
items.text: Access to different service domains at the same time, separated by the provider's policies.

items.title: Policy and quality of service
items.text: Easier assignment of policy and quality of service based on the subscribed services.

items.title: Default service
items.text: With no service named, the home agent acts as if plain Internet access had been requested.
